title: Portfolio Website
description: A modern, data-driven React portfolio with polished navigation, scroll-based visual effects, reusable components, and recruiter-focused content architecture.
details: Built 6 routed portfolio areas with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router, and ReactBits-inspired visual components.
Implemented interactive Galaxy and SideRays backgrounds, collapsible navigation, scroll-controlled rocket motion, responsive pages, and JSON-driven content.
Structured projects, internships, extracurriculars, contact details, and CV access through reusable page components and centralized data files.

title: Foolics API - Online Food Ordering Backend System
description: A Foodics internship backend API for an online ordering system, built to support a separate frontend team with documented auth, cart, order, stock, and admin workflows.
details: Developed Express REST APIs covering user registration/login, product lookup, cart management, order creation, admin dashboard data, stock updates, and order-status transitions.
Integrated PostgreSQL with Prisma models for users, carts, cart items, products, orders, and order items, with JWT authentication and admin authorization middleware.
Documented the API with Swagger UI, added Jest and Supertest coverage for core endpoint workflows, and provided Docker setup for handoff to the frontend team.

details: Designed and implemented automated conveyor belt control logic using FPGA and VHDL.

title: Operating System Simulator
description: A C-based simulation of monolithic operating system concepts with process scheduling, memory management, disk swapping, and resource mutexes.
details: Built a custom text-based program interpreter for OS course workflows.
Implemented process scheduling, memory management, disk swapping, and synchronized resource access with mutex-style controls.
Compared multiple scheduling algorithms and simulated core monolithic OS behavior through controlled test programs.

title: Computer Architecture Processor
description: A C-based simulation of a pipelined Harvard Architecture processor for the Computer Systems Architecture course at GUC.
details: Implemented a custom 16-bit instruction set architecture for the Double McHarvard processor specification.
Built a 3-stage instruction pipeline with hazard handling and separated instruction/data memory behavior.
Simulated instruction execution to verify register, memory, and pipeline-state behavior.

details: Built a 4-role front-end prototype with authentication, protected routes, dashboards, portfolio browsing, course workflows, messaging, and notifications.
Implemented student, instructor, employer, and admin experiences using React Router, local state, dummy data, charts, and reusable layout components.
Captured a local walkthrough covering login, project browsing, and statistics screens.

title: Tomasulo Algorithm Simulator
description: An interactive, cycle-by-cycle MIPS assembly simulator using Tomasulo's algorithm for Microprocessors (CSEN 702), with loops, integer operations, and floating-point execution.
details: Implemented dynamic instruction scheduling and register renaming to handle RAW, WAR, and WAW hazards, with arbitration for competing Common Data Bus results.
Modeled a configurable data cache and byte-addressable memory with hit/miss timing and load/store address-conflict handling.
Integrated a two-bit branch predictor with instruction flushing on misprediction and an in-order pipeline mode for comparison with out-of-order execution.
Visualized reservation stations, load/store buffers, register files, cache contents, and instruction queues, with configurable latencies and hardware capacities.

title: RPS Guardian - Vision-Based Robotic Hand
description: Developing an ARM-based robotic hand that plays Rock-Paper-Scissors through camera-based gesture recognition and servo-controlled fingers for Embedded Systems Architecture (CSEN 701).
details: Developing C/C++ firmware using the Raspberry Pi Pico SDK and modular drivers for an analog force sensor through ADC, a keypad and limit switches through GPIO, and a DC reward-drawer motor through an H-bridge.
Integrating C++ vision processing over USB serial, using timestamps and round IDs to synchronize gesture capture, robotic movement, and scoring while rejecting stale or duplicate results.
Designing dual-core processing with a synchronized bounded queue to separate communication handling from game timing and actuator control.

Completed modeling of six concurrent subsystems in MATLAB/Simulink Stateflow using hierarchical state machines and event broadcasting, including motion-stop handling, communication faults, and motor timeout recovery; firmware and hardware integration remain in progress.

title: Ninja Turtles - 2D Defense Game & 3D World Exploration
description: A Computer Graphics project combining a Ninja Turtles-themed 2D tower defense game with interactive 3D world exploration using C++, OpenGL 3.3, GLSL, and GLM.
details: Implemented lane-based combat with AABB collision detection, melee and projectile attacks, defensive shields, and progressively challenging enemy waves.
Built two explorable 3D environments with imported textured models, model transformations, and custom vertex and fragment shaders using directional, point, and spotlight lighting.
Implemented first-person and third-person cameras, top/front/side views, frame-rate-independent movement, and object interactions triggered by proximity and viewing angle.
Created keyframe-based cutscenes and coordinated horror effects combining camera movement, dynamic lighting, and object animation.

title: University Schedule Management System
description: Collaborating in a ten-member team on a full-stack MERN academic scheduling and advising platform for Advanced Computer Lab.
details: Developing dedicated dashboards for four user roles with JWT authentication and backend role-based access control.
Implementing course offerings, timetable templates, enrollment, and student assignments with room/instructor conflict detection and seat-capacity validation.
Using MongoDB transactions and conditional atomic updates to keep schedules and seat allocations consistent during concurrent requests.
Developing schedule swaps, extra credit-hour approvals, eligibility checks, course pricing, and academic-history access with PDF transcripts and CSV activity exports.

title: Jackaroo Board Game
description: A single-player Java Jackaroo board game applying object-oriented programming, data structures, and algorithms.
details: Designed a modular game engine using interfaces, inheritance, enums, and exception handling to enforce complex game rules.
Implemented movement validation, swapping, traps, and safe zones with turn-based gameplay and AI players.
